summary.text: Chris Moore is One Nation's candidate for Greenvale at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC he has lived in Greenvale all his life, has worked for over 20 years in civil construction, infrastructure and project management, and volunteers as a CFA firefighter.

occupation.text: Civil construction, infrastructure and project management

sources.title: Greenvale: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Declan McGinness is the Greens candidate for Greenvale at the 2026 Victorian election. He lives in Westmeadows, has led operations at Ronald McDonald House and has managed an optometry store. He stood for the Greens in Niddrie at the 2022 state election and has held leadership roles in the party.

occupation.text: Community services and retail management (operations lead at Ronald McDonald House; optometry retail manager)

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia's results table names the Greens candidate 'Dylan McGinness' but cites the Greens' page for Declan McGinness as a candidate for this ward; he lost the two-candidate count to Labor's Phil Burn.

priorities.text: I want to be a representative who listens
Encouraging residents to volunteer and speak up on local issues

sources.title: Greenvale: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Declan McGinness, Candidate for Greenvale, Australian Greens

summary.text: Iwan Walters has been the Labor member for Greenvale in the Legislative Assembly since the new seat was first contested in 2022. He taught at a secondary school in country Victoria and later did research in the United Kingdom on training and job pathways for young people. He is recontesting Greenvale in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Secondary school teacher in country Victoria
Researcher in the UK on youth training and employment

priorities.text: Good education for young people wherever they live
A fairer share of prosperity, including for outer suburbs

sources.title: Iwan Walters, Parliament of Victoria
Iwan Walters, Wikipedia

summary.text: Jim Overend is the Liberal candidate for Greenvale at the 2026 Victorian election. A Hume City councillor for about six years, he lives in Craigieburn and has been in Melbourne's north for more than 40 years. Before council he ran a small business selling road safety products and worked in business development.

prior_roles.role: Owner-operator of a road safety supplies business

prior_roles.organisation: Craigieburn Car, Truck and Bike Show

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia describes him as an 'Independent Liberal' at this election; council ballots carry no party names.

priorities.text: Better roads and infrastructure in the north

sources.title: Greenvale: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Jim Overend, Liberal for Greenvale, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Kirill Smelov is standing for the Victorian Socialists in Greenvale at the 2026 state election. He works in IT locally and is a union member who has organised workers over pay and conditions. He says he has also campaigned against racism, for climate action and in support of Palestinians.

priorities.text: I believe in a society that puts people before profit
Properly funded public services, with hospitals and schools within easy reach
Giving residents' worries about local parks and the environment more weight than developers' interests

sources.title: Greenvale: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Kirill Smelov, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Mazen Yohanna is the Citizens Party candidate for Greenvale at the 2026 Victorian election; the party's page for him gives his name as Mazen Yohanna. He came to Australia from Iraq with his family during the First Gulf War, speaks four languages and says he has long volunteered for the Citizens Party. After jobs including security work and quality control for Ford and Toyota, he now cares full time for his daughter.

priorities.text: I am passionate to fix the road quality, improve school zone parking
Brighter street lighting so local streets are safer at night
Bringing back a public bank, including the party's post office bank policy
Having government build housing and infrastructure directly rather than through private outsourcing

sources.title: Greenvale: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Mazen John, Citizens Party Victoria

summary.text: Rosanna Furina is standing for the Animal Justice Party in Greenvale at the 2026 Victorian election, as she did in 2022. She has worked as an interior designer and in the construction industry, and her party says she has eaten a plant-based diet since 2016 and supported local animal protection campaigns.

occupation.text: Interior designer; has also worked in the construction industry

priorities.text: Stronger protection for animals and the environment in Victoria
Legislating to end cruel practices that are standard in animal agriculture
Action to slow environmental damage and the climate crisis
